prompt: A superball is dropped from rest onto a hard floor and bounces back up to nearly its original height. Neglecting air resistance and taking vertically upwards as the positive direction, which description matches its velocity-time graph during the drop, bounce, and rebound?
options: A line with negative gradient below the time axis, an instantaneous vertical jump across the axis, then a parallel line with negative gradient above the axis towards zero.
A horizontal line at negative value, a jump to positive value, and a horizontal line at positive value.
A line with positive gradient above the time axis, an instantaneous jump downwards, then a line below the axis.
A continuous parabola starting at the origin and curving smoothly back to zero.

answer.explanation: Taking upwards as positive, downward free fall has negative velocity increasing in magnitude with constant negative acceleration -g (gradient -9.81 m s^-2). During contact with the floor, velocity reverses rapidly to a positive value. During upward flight, velocity is positive and decreases with the exact same negative gradient -g towards zero.

distractor_explanations: Correct. Falling gives v < 0 with gradient -g; after rebound v > 0 with identical gradient -g decreasing to zero.
Incorrect. Assumes velocities are constant rather than uniformly accelerated by gravity.
Incorrect. Confuses upward and downward signs for velocity.
Incorrect. Describes a displacement-time curve rather than a velocity-time graph.
hints: Determine the sign of the velocity when moving downwards and when moving upwards.
What is the acceleration during free fall in both upward and downward phases when upwards is positive?
solution: A. A line with negative gradient below the time axis, an instantaneous vertical jump across the axis, then a parallel line with negative gradient above the axis towards zero.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Falling: u = 0, object moves downwards so v < 0. Acceleration is downward, so gradient dv/dt = -g.
Step 2: Impact: short contact time causes velocity to reverse from negative to positive.
Step 3: Rebound: object moves upwards so v > 0. Acceleration is still downward gravity, so gradient dv/dt = -g.
Step 4: Both straight line sections have the identical gradient of -9.81 m s^-2.
